findings.title: Unguarded property access on possibly-undefined first destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` can yield `undefined` when the array is empty or null, but the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. For any event with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar (for example a user with no destinationCalendar set), `create()` throws a TypeError and the booking fails. It should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Inverted condition for organization slug (and requestedSlug) after refactor
findings.body: The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })`. The rewrite to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` and `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {}` flips the logic. When billing is disabled the org is no longer created with its slug, and when billing is enabled the slug is written to the wrong field. This is unrelated to the PR's stated goal and changes org creation behavior.

findings.title: updateEvent calendar lookup returns undefined when no externalCalendarId is passed
findings.body: The fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined), this searches for a destination whose externalId equals null/undefined, which never matches. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. So `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined and `calendar.events.update` is called with no calendarId, which breaks updates for bookings lacking an external calendar id. The same faulty `find` is repeated in deleteEvent (around line 317), where it causes the calendarId to fall back to 'primary' instead of the booking's calendar.

findings.title: Calendar references lose externalCalendarId for non-destination-specific creates
findings.body: `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined` relies on `createEvent` returning `externalId`. But in `createAllCalendarEvents`, the branch without `destination.credentialId` calls `createEvent(c, event)` with no externalId, and the fallback branch does the same. Those results have `externalId` undefined, so the stored BookingReference has no externalCalendarId. Previously it was taken from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Later reschedule, cancel, and update operations then target the wrong or default calendar.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes the same events once per calendar reference
findings.body: The calendar references are now iterated with `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. In the recurring-all-remaining branch, the inner logic loops over every `updatedBookings` and every calendar credential and deletes each one. With N calendar references, each remaining event is deleted N times, producing duplicate deleteEvent calls and duplicate pushes into apiDeletes. The recurring branch should run once, not once per reference.

findings.title: loadUsers error mapping misclassifies errors and turns a missing-list case into a hard failure
findings.body: The rewritten loadUsers throws a plain Error when dynamicUserList is empty or not an array. That plain Error is not an HttpError, so the catch converts it to a 500 'Unable to load users'. The catch also maps `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` (a database failure) to a 400 Bad Request, which blames the client for server-side errors. Previously an empty list just returned no users. This changes status codes and error semantics in the booking path.

findings.title: Dynamic user query dropped the organization select
findings.body: The rewritten `findMany` for dynamic users removed the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` clause that was in the original query. Any downstream code that reads `organization.slug` from these users will now get undefined. The removal is not explained by the PR's description.

findings.title: Team collective calendars are silently dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destinationCalendar. Later, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op in that case, so the collective team members' calendars are never added and those hosts are not invited on their calendars. The array should be initialized as `[]` and the team calendars appended regardless.

findings.title: createEvent passes credentialId but Google createEvent's calendarId falls back inconsistently between insert and patch
findings.body: In the Google createEvent path, insert uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` uses the raw `selectedCalendar`, which can be undefined. When the patch is issued for a hangoutLink event without a matched destination calendar, the patch targets an undefined calendarId and fails silently, because its errors are not handled.
